title: How Scott Wu uses Devin as an async junior engineer: tasks not problems, sync-then-async handoff
summary: Scott Wu, CEO of Cognition, demos how his team works with Devin as a junior engineer teammate. Scope work as clear tasks, do a short synchronous research-and-prompt step, then hand off async, and make Devin the default first responder in public Slack threads. He also shares his top Devin use cases and a voice-in-meetings habit.

principles.text: Give AI agents tasks, not problems. Clear, well-specified tasks are where a junior-level agent shines.
principles.quote: where Devon really shines is one way that we say it also is is kind of like tasks not problems.

principles.text: Split work into a short sync phase (research, spec the prompt) and then an async handoff, like briefing an intern for two minutes.
principles.quote: for a lot of tasks there's often this sync component like the synchronous component and then this asynchronous component, right? And a lot of what search and wiki is for is for for doing the synchronous part of the task before you do the async

principles.text: Async agents let you run many tasks in parallel and check in later, which suits people stuck in meetings.
principles.quote: For better or for worse, I'm in meetings for a lot of the day and it's it's it's great to be able to just kind of kick these off

principles.text: Institutionalize the agent as first responder: tag it first on every issue, crash and request in shared Slack channels.
principles.quote: it's almost just like institutionalizing Devon as first line of response is how I would describe it.

principles.text: Work with the agent in multiplayer threads: knowledge compounds for the agent and teammates learn from each other.
principles.quote: Devon is a naturally multiplayer experience

principles.text: When an agent gets stuck, review its step history to find what it missed, then re-instruct it, like pair debugging with an intern.
principles.quote: it's kind of like pair pair programming or pair debugging with an intern.
